title: Home robot R1 — round body, D200 LiDAR and one camera

parts.item: NVIDIA Jetson Nano assembly
parts.notes: Keep the existing carrier, module and heatsink. CAD = NVIDIA's official Jetson Nano Developer Kit P3450 B01 STEP (reference-models/jetson-nano-b01, simplified by cad/simplify_jetson.py): carrier 100 × 79 mm, heatsink top 28.3 mm above the PCB, I/O row (barrel jack, HDMI + DP, 2 × stacked USB-A, RJ45, micro-USB) on the 100 mm edge facing forward (+x), barrel jack on the right; carrier PCB underside z 57 over the motors. Four Ø2.75 mounting holes on 86 × 58 mm (hole pattern from the STEP) at (25, -46), (-33, -46), (25, 40), (-33, 40) on H05 standoffs: two 24 mm stacks from P_base (front) and two 20 mm F-F standoffs on the bay board, which they clamp (rear). Check that the owned board is a B01 (two CSI connectors); an A02 has one CSI connector and other port positions. Barrel-jack power needs the J48 jumper fitted; the 5 V barrel lead assumes the 4 GB kit (a 2 GB kit needs its specified USB-C input). An Orin requires a revised power design. Assembly order (bay board under the Jetson): 0. on the bench, make the two motor pigtails (C18) and plug them on. They differ in length and in pin-1 order, so tag each one "L / J4" (left motor) or "R / J5" (right motor) right after making it, before it is plugged on. The pre-cut length of the six wires of each pigtail is 61 mm for J4 (left) and 57 mm for J5 (right): the drawn route + terminations + the full 12.7 mm pin spread, rounded up to the mm, because the six wires fan out 6.35 mm either side of the bundle's centre line at both ends (the socket's six sleeves and the male housing's six cavities each span 12.7 mm). Solder the socket end first (one wire lapped on each solder tail of the right-angle socket under its Ø1.8 sleeve, red wire on pin 1, the tails and wires pointing up), then push the socket onto its header; leave the male ends long: they are dressed along the route, trimmed to length and crimped in step 4. J4 pin 1 = rear end, J5 pin 1 = front end (the square pads); the pigtails are built alike, so the rule is the same for both: looking into the socket's mating face with its tails up, the red wire (pin 1) is on the left. The pigtails stay with the board. Power connectors (ruling PB30): the battery (J1, an AMASS XT30 PCB male), the master rocker (J2, a JST VH header) and the Jetson 5 V (J3, a Molex Micro-Fit 3.0 right-angle header) are three different connector families, so no lead fits a wrong header; tag the three leads anyway ("J1 BATT", "J2 ROCKER", "J3 JETSON 5V") right after making them. Battery lead polarity: J1 pin 1 is GND (silk "-") and pin 2 is BAT+ (silk "+"), so the lead's XT30U-F carries GND in cavity 1 (its "-" contact: battery -, black) and BAT+ in cavity 2 (its "+" contact: battery +, red); the XT30 mates only one way round, but a lead soldered the wrong way round still mates. Check it fail-safe before the fuses go in: with F1 and F2 out, plug W01 into J1 and into the battery and measure F1's input clip (its BAT+ side, F1 pin 1) against a GND pad (TP5 or an M3 hole ring): it must read positive, about the pack voltage (≥ 6 V; a part-discharged pack reads lower); a reversed lead reads negative and, with the fuses out, has no current path. Only then fit the fuses, always with the rocker off (F1 first, F2 last): a reversed lead with the fuses in is the costliest mistake on this board (it has no reverse-polarity protection); 1. bond the two printed bearing ribs into their 0.6 mm locating pockets in the P_base top with epoxy (F04) and let it cure; fit the two front Jetson standoffs (24 mm stacks), screwed from below; 2. set the four 2.4 mm printed spacers and the two printed clamp spacers on P_base, lower the bay board onto them and screw it down with four M3 × 8 pan-head screws into the inserts; 3. fit the battery tray (its hold-down beams freed: breakaway posts cut): set it 2 mm aft of its place, slide it forward so its three spring fingers ride up their lead-ins onto the board's top face between the rear connectors, screw it down, and check each finger stands lifted: a 0.05 mm feeler does not pass under its tip; if it does, that finger has play (it is off the board): stick 0.1 mm PTFE tape (F03) under its tip as a shim, a layer at a time (about 0.3 mm at most), until the feeler no longer passes; 4. plug the under-carrier cables. Pigtails: dress each one as drawn, with no slack (it rides up with the board when the joint is unplugged): straight up out of the socket, toward the front about 12 mm over the board beside U5A (J9 on the right), out between the P03 and the motor face, and down to the inline joint just ahead of the motor (x 15.2..17.8, |y| 38..60); then trim each wire at its own cavity of the male housing (finished lengths 35.4–60.8 mm for J4 and 31.1–56.5 mm for J5, set by where each wire sits at both ends) and crimp its male pin into the 1×6 housing, red wire = pin 1. Factory cables: measure each one from the encoder cap to the female housing's rear face (the wire entry); readings of 186–200 mm all fit (2–3 turns), and a longer cable up to 220 mm still fits (up to 3.5 turns). Route the fixed path first (about 89 mm outside the coil): a flat row along the motor's inner end face toward the rear, round the motor's rear shoulder and forward over the motor top (never over the pigtail), down the motor's front shoulder under the bumper lead, and from the coil position into the housing; wind the remainder (the measured length less the fixed path: 97–111 mm) into the coil on the base ahead of the motor (2–3.5 turns, about 16 mm across, at x 25, |y| 72) and tie it through its two slots. Then mate each motor's factory female housing onto its pigtail's male housing: the joint is not keyed, so mate the pin-1 stripe to the pin-1 stripe (both halves are marked at the red wire) and check the colours run straight across; stand the joint on the base and tie it down with a cable tie down the motor opening and up through the slot beside it; bumpers J10/J11; front cliffs J8/J9; 5. set and verify the P03 output voltage on the bench, connect it to U5A/U5B (pin 1 is "+" on both terminals, silk "+", the screw nearer the robot centre line: U5A.1 to P03 IN+, U5B.1 to P03 OUT+, red wires on pin 1), then fit it on its foam tape in the front bay with the cable tie through the P_base slots at (28, ±33.3); before the Jetson is connected (W04 unplugged): battery in, F1 fitted, rocker on, and measure against a GND pad: U5A.1 reads positive, about the pack voltage, and U5B.1 positive 5.1 V (0 V or negative: the P03 leads are swapped or loose); then rocker off; 6. stand the two rear 20 mm F-F standoffs on the board and screw each down with an M2.5 × 12 countersunk screw from under P_base through the base, the clamp spacer and the board (they clamp the board); 7. fit the Jetson (four M2.5 top screws), then its six plugs; before the 5 V barrel plug goes in, check the Jetson lead W04 on J3 with its barrel plug free and the rocker on: the plug's centre reads positive 5.1 V against its sleeve (negative: the two Micro-Fit crimps are swapped), then rocker off and plug it in. Service: step 0, every time, before reaching inside: shut the Jetson down, switch the rocker off and unplug the battery (BAT+ is live and unfused at F1's input whenever the battery is plugged in). Everyday rule: the rocker off before plugging or unplugging the battery; shut the Jetson down before switching the rocker off; fit or pull a fuse only with the rocker off (rocker off, fit F2, rocker on). With the lid off, the board's rear band (Pico USB, rear connector row, the Jetson 5 V lead J3, fuses) is reachable; the motor inline joints, the other under-carrier connectors and the P03 (tie, trimpot) need the Jetson off (its six plugs: camera, LiDAR and Pico USB, Wi-Fi dongle, 5 V barrel plug, fan; then its four top screws). To take the board out: Jetson off; the two rear standoffs off (their M2.5 screws from under P_base); the battery out (strap, Tamiya plug); the four tray screws out, the tray slid 2 mm aft and lifted straight out (its springs come off the board edge; its walls are cut clear of the rear cliff sensor boards); the four M3 board screws out; unplug the rear-band plugs, the motor inline joints (loosen each factory-cable coil tie first: the 8 mm each housing slides back comes out of the coil; then cut the joint ties and slide each factory housing off its pigtail; the pigtails stay on J4 / J5 and ride up with the board), the bumper and front cliff leads and the P03 leads; lift the board. Fit new ties when it goes back (retie the coils).

parts.item: Raspberry Pi Pico RP2040
parts.notes: Two purchased July 2022; install one, keep the other as spare. Supplied from Jetson USB only. 51 × 21 mm board.

parts.item: HiLetgo GY-521 MPU-6050
parts.notes: August 2019 purchase. Use a 3.3 V I2C bus; check the actual breakout regulator/pullups. CAD uses an estimated 21 × 16 × 8 mm envelope.

parts.item: Waveshare OV2735 2MP USB Camera (A), SKU 33122
parts.notes: Single 25 x 25 mm USB camera; 1080p30, 5 V. Video and future recognition only; no stereo depth. Camera board, lens depth and USB position require actual fit check. Listed price checked 2026-10-03. Task N (LIO-134): the white LED E19 sits above the lens on a printed shelf (P_camera_led_shelf) clamped under the two upper board screws (M2 × 8, see H09).

parts.item: Samsung LM281B+ Pro 2835 white LED, 5000 K, CRI 80 (SPMWH1228MD5WAR0VK)
parts.notes: Task N (LIO-134): one white LED above the front camera lens, facing forward, so the camera has light on the floor and the band in front of the robot in a dark corner. Datasheet values: 37.5 lm at 65 mA, forward voltage 2.7 V, beam angle 120°. Run from J15 pin 5 (5 V) through a 39 Ω resistor: (5 − 2.7) / 39 = 59 mA, so about 37.5 × 59 / 65 = 34 lm and about 10.8 cd on the axis; 0.16 W in the LED, 0.14 W in the resistor, about 0.30 W in all. Emitting face at x 145.8, y 0, z 89.45 mm; the light leaves through the existing camera window in the bumper. A 2.8 × 3.5 × 0.8 mm SMD part: solder it across the cut of the carrier E20 and mind its polarity mark (BRINGUP.md section 10 item 6). On while a task drives, off when idle; no PWM dimming (a rolling-shutter camera would show bands). The price is an estimate; the second LED is a spare for a burnt one. The figures are on the verify list.

parts.item: Camera LED carrier: 10 × 3.1 mm piece of 0.8 mm single-sided copper-clad board
parts.notes: Task N (LIO-134). Cut a piece 10 × 3.1 mm from single-sided copper-clad board (0.8 mm as modelled; check another thickness against the shelf). Split the copper into two pads with a knife cut about 0.5 mm wide across the middle; scrape until a meter shows no connection between the pads. Solder the LED (E19) across the cut, one terminal on each pad, then solder the two wires (26 AWG) to the pads beside the LED and lead them back along the shelf block's sides (keep them under the carrier's top edge: the bumper seam backer passes 2.1 mm over it). Mark the anode pad (BRINGUP.md section 10 item 6). Glue the carrier's back face to the front face of the printed shelf P_camera_led_shelf (epoxy F04 or cyanoacrylate). The price is an estimate for a small sheet; most of it is left over.

parts.item: Pololu 4867, 99:1 MP 12 V encoder gearmotor
parts.notes: USD 53.95 each. 25 mm diameter; about 69 mm body plus 12.5 mm shaft. 4 mm D-shaft. Nominal 79 RPM at 12 V; approximately 47 RPM unloaded at 7.2 V is an estimate. Encoder supply must be at least 3.5 V: the board feeds it 5 V and reads A / B through the 2N7002 input stages. Factory 200 mm 6-lead cable with a 1×6 0.1 in female housing (red motor +, black motor −, green encoder GND, blue encoder VCC, yellow A, white B): it is not cut; it mates with the C18 pigtail at the inline joint ahead of the motor. Measure each cable from the encoder cap to the female housing's rear face (the wire entry): the vendor's "200 mm" is on the verify list, and readings of 186–200 mm all fit. Route the fixed path first and wind the remainder into a 2–3 turn coil on the base and tie it (assembly step 4); loosen the coil tie before unplugging the inline joint. Vendor STEP included as a reference.

parts.item: Pololu 4035 DRV8874 single brushed DC motor driver carrier
parts.notes: One per motor, plugged into the bay board sockets U3L / U3P (left) and U4L / U4P (right), turned 180 deg in place (rulings PB15 / PB16: logic row toward the Pico). 4.5–37 V, 2.1 A continuous, about 1.1 V/A current sense, default current limit about 4.4 A (pcb/reference/pololu-4035.txt). Firmware limits each channel to 1.8 A continuous (BRINGUP-NOTES). Solder the supplied male header strips with the components up. USD 11.94 each (B9 review; verify on the order page).

parts.item: Pololu 3690, 80 × 10 mm multi-hub wheels
parts.notes: Use included 4 mm D collets, plates and six M3 × 7 screws. No additional hubs needed.

parts.item: Pololu 2692, 1 inch ball caster with bearings
parts.notes: ONE rear caster (no front support): ball centre at x = -75 mm behind the axle; the caster carries about 0.22 of the weight and the rear cliff sensors (-110, ±81) lead it by 35 mm in reverse. DriveCore disarms on a hazard and the robot coasts on the motor dynamic brake: from the 0.06 m/s firmware reverse speed limit (parameters.json reverse_speed_limit_m_s; required) that needs 23.4 mm (14.7 mm coast, no rolling drag, conservative), so no active brake is required (validation caster_layout.stopping); reversing faster than 0.095 m/s would not be covered. 29 mm assembled height. CAD housing is a conservative envelope; three M3 × 5 pan-head machine screws (H13) on a 16.5 mm bolt circle, outside the Ø25.4 ball, through the 2 mm flange tabs into M3 brass heat-set inserts (H12) pressed into P_base from below. Drill the flange tabs to this pattern if the purchased caster differs.

parts.item: Tenergy 7.2 V 3800 mAh NiMH flat battery
parts.notes: Two packs and charger purchased March 2021. Install only ONE pack; second stays off robot as spare. Working envelope 140 × 50 × 27 mm, based on the 11200 family with clearance. Confirm actual pack, connector polarity and capacity.

parts.item: Existing matching NiMH charger
parts.notes: Charge the removed, disconnected pack using its matching NiMH charger. No onboard charging or docking in R1.

parts.item: Automotive blade fuses: 7.5 A main and 5 A motor
parts.notes: ATO blade fuses for the bay board's FLR holders: 7.5 A in F1 (main), 5 A in F2 (motor branch), plus a spare of each: e.g. Littelfuse 0287007.PXCN / 0287005.PXCN (verify). Verify the start-up current against the 5 A motor fuse.

parts.item: SPST master rocker switch, ≥10 A at 12 VDC
parts.notes: Select a documented DC-rated snap-in rocker whose datasheet panel thickness range includes 1.5 mm; the CAD envelope is a 12.6 × 19.8 × 25 mm body (z 78.5–103.5) through a 13.2 × 20.4 mm printed opening in the lid top at (-100, 0), with a 15.7 × 24.4 × 1.5 mm relief pocket under the lid so the panel is 1.5 mm at the opening (check the fit on P_coupon first; file to the datasheet panel cut-out so the snap tabs hold), plus a 24 × 21 × 3 mm bezel on the lid. The old rear panel is now inside the rear shell. Switch off after the Jetson has shut down.

parts.item: 100 nF ceramic suppression capacitor
parts.notes: Across each motor’s terminals; short leads. Additional 100 nF capacitor in the battery sense filter is listed with signal components.

parts.item: Maintained SPST motor-power mini-toggle switch
parts.notes: Planning allowance. Select contacts rated for at least 0.5 A at 12 V DC. Interrupts the 5 V relay coil only; OFF disconnects motor supply while Jetson stays powered. CAD assumes a 6.0 mm bushing through a 6.6 mm printed lid hole (ream to the datasheet panel hole) and a 13 x 8 x 14 mm body; match actual drawing before printing.

parts.item: Momentary normally-open arm button
parts.notes: 12 mm panel mount, low voltage, through a 12.6 mm printed lid hole (ream to the datasheet size). Connect to Pico input and ground; firmware must require deliberate arming.

parts.item: Omron SS-5GL2 hinge roller lever microswitch
parts.notes: Front left/right contact bumpers. Use COM + NC so an open wire also requests a stop. SS-5GL2 is the HINGE ROLLER lever (Ø4.8 × 3.2 roller on a 14.5 mm lever; Omron SS datasheet: OF max 0.49 N, FP max 19.3 mm, OP 14.5 ± 0.8 mm, OT min 1.2 mm, MD max 0.8 mm, heights of the roller top above the mounting-hole line). Each switch hangs under P_base on two M2 × 14 screws with washers and nuts on the base top, through 2.4 mm slots that let it slide ±0.9 mm along its own Y axis, turned 30° so the roller runs along the half's travel. The rail cam holds the roller above the release position at rest; the roller meets the 40° ramp from about 0 mm of travel and a dwell holds it past OP to the 5 mm stop. Because the OP tolerance (±0.8 mm) exceeds OT min (1.2 mm), the switch is set at assembly (from above, in the front bay): hold the half 2.25 mm in (gauge block at the rest stop; the roller force holds the bearing on its slot side), slide the switch toward the cam until it just operates, tighten. During a hit the bearing can cross its slot (up to 2 × 0.1 mm), which makes the switch operate earlier, never later: operation stays within 1.99–2.25 mm for slot widths 8.1–8.2 mm (validation.json bumper_travel.switch.slot_width_cases). Confirm the allowed dog direction with Omron's precautions (the cam meets the roller from the lever-tip side).

parts.item: Pololu VL53L0X carrier, item 2490
parts.notes: USD 19.95 each checked 2026-10-03. Downward-facing sensors, optical face about 42.5 mm above the floor: front (105, ±72), rear (-110, ±81) beside the battery tray. VIN 3.3 V; XSHUT driven LOW or high impedance only. Reassign I2C addresses at boot. Test on actual floors; loss of reading requests stop.

parts.item: 64 GB UHS-I microSD card
parts.notes: Reuse installed card if healthy and large enough; storage is not confirmed in purchase history. Included inside the Jetson assembly envelope.

parts.item: Compatible USB Wi-Fi adapter
parts.notes: Exact adapter/chipset depends on the Jetson image. CAD reserves a compact USB dongle plus plug access; choose a supported model after identifying the existing adapter.

parts.item: 40 × 40 × 10 mm 5 V fan with matching Jetson lead
parts.notes: Use existing cooler if present. Fan header/plug depends on board revision. CAD: 40 × 40 × 10 mm fan (Ø34 bore) on the heatsink 32 mm screw pattern with four M3 pan-head screws (heads ≤ Ø5.6 × 2.1 mm). The LiDAR tray seals its intake (task L; until then a skirt under the lid): its 1.3 mm duct round the Ø35 fan window and the LD14 motor ends 0.9 mm above the fan frame, 0.51 mm from the screw heads (check the gap at assembly with modelling clay, BRINGUP section 10: 0.5–1.0 mm; a fan with a bore over Ø35 or larger screw heads needs the duct re-checked). Lid-on load test before the robot is used: lid, LiDAR and tray fitted, sustained full CPU + GPU load for 20 min, log tegrastats (CPU/GPU/SoC temperatures and clocks) and compare with a lid-off run; the lid passes if the clocks never throttle. Carry into pcb/BRINGUP.md (L11).

parts.item: USB 2.0 data cable, Type-A to Type-C, 0.5 m
parts.status: Check camera bundle; budget to buy
parts.notes: Single camera to Jetson. Buy a complete 0.5 m data cable; never cut USB cables to the harness estimate. Charge-only cables are unsuitable. Connector orientation and strain relief are represented as envelopes.

parts.item: USB data cable, Type-A to Micro-B, 0.5 m
parts.notes: Jetson to Pico. Pico receives power through this cable; do not also connect external 5 V to its VBUS.

parts.item: 5.5 × 2.1 mm DC barrel plug lead, ≥4 A, 18 AWG
parts.notes: Conditional on original Nano 4 GB barrel input: 5 V, center positive, appropriate power-select jumper. For Nano 2 GB replace with a suitable 5 V/3 A USB-C power lead. Never connect battery voltage directly.

parts.item: Standard Tamiya mating connector / pigtail
parts.notes: Match actual battery housing, contact gender and polarity. Keep the existing battery connector intact. 18 AWG or heavier.

parts.item: JST VH 2-position housing and contacts (VHR-2N + SVH-21T-P1.1)
parts.notes: Mate for the bay board's B2P-VH header J2 (the header is E18): the master rocker pair W02. J2 is the board's only VH header (ruling PB30: J1 is an XT30, C19; J3 a Micro-Fit 3.0, C20), so the rocker pair fits no other header. 18 AWG; crimp with a JST-type crimper; buy spare contacts.

parts.item: M2.5 screws + nylon standoffs, front: two 24 mm stacks (12 mm M-F + 12 mm F-F) + four M2.5 × 6 pan-head carrier screws
parts.notes: Front: two 24 mm M2.5 nylon standoff stacks from P_base to the Jetson carrier, each a 12 mm M-F (female end down, male stud up) under a 12 mm F-F, so both ends are female, on M2.5 × 8 countersunk screws from under P_base (flush in 90 deg countersinks). (A one-piece stock 25 mm F-F would raise the carrier to z 58; the CAD keeps z 57.) Four M2.5 × 6 pan-head screws hold the carrier on all four standoffs from the top (the two rear ones are H14). Jetson B01 mounting holes Ø2.75 on 86 × 58 mm (hole pattern taken from NVIDIA's STEP) at (25, -46), (-33, -46), (25, 40), (-33, 40). Carrier underside z 57: 4.5 mm over the motor tops (through-hole leads reach 1.9 mm under the PCB); Jetson isolated from P_base. Assembly order (bay board under the Jetson): 0. on the bench, make the two motor pigtails (C18) and plug them on. They differ in length and in pin-1 order, so tag each one "L / J4" (left motor) or "R / J5" (right motor) right after making it, before it is plugged on. The pre-cut length of the six wires of each pigtail is 61 mm for J4 (left) and 57 mm for J5 (right): the drawn route + terminations + the full 12.7 mm pin spread, rounded up to the mm, because the six wires fan out 6.35 mm either side of the bundle's centre line at both ends (the socket's six sleeves and the male housing's six cavities each span 12.7 mm). Solder the socket end first (one wire lapped on each solder tail of the right-angle socket under its Ø1.8 sleeve, red wire on pin 1, the tails and wires pointing up), then push the socket onto its header; leave the male ends long: they are dressed along the route, trimmed to length and crimped in step 4. J4 pin 1 = rear end, J5 pin 1 = front end (the square pads); the pigtails are built alike, so the rule is the same for both: looking into the socket's mating face with its tails up, the red wire (pin 1) is on the left. The pigtails stay with the board. Power connectors (ruling PB30): the battery (J1, an AMASS XT30 PCB male), the master rocker (J2, a JST VH header) and the Jetson 5 V (J3, a Molex Micro-Fit 3.0 right-angle header) are three different connector families, so no lead fits a wrong header; tag the three leads anyway ("J1 BATT", "J2 ROCKER", "J3 JETSON 5V") right after making them. Battery lead polarity: J1 pin 1 is GND (silk "-") and pin 2 is BAT+ (silk "+"), so the lead's XT30U-F carries GND in cavity 1 (its "-" contact: battery -, black) and BAT+ in cavity 2 (its "+" contact: battery +, red); the XT30 mates only one way round, but a lead soldered the wrong way round still mates. Check it fail-safe before the fuses go in: with F1 and F2 out, plug W01 into J1 and into the battery and measure F1's input clip (its BAT+ side, F1 pin 1) against a GND pad (TP5 or an M3 hole ring): it must read positive, about the pack voltage (≥ 6 V; a part-discharged pack reads lower); a reversed lead reads negative and, with the fuses out, has no current path. Only then fit the fuses, always with the rocker off (F1 first, F2 last): a reversed lead with the fuses in is the costliest mistake on this board (it has no reverse-polarity protection); 1. bond the two printed bearing ribs into their 0.6 mm locating pockets in the P_base top with epoxy (F04) and let it cure; fit the two front Jetson standoffs (24 mm stacks), screwed from below; 2. set the four 2.4 mm printed spacers and the two printed clamp spacers on P_base, lower the bay board onto them and screw it down with four M3 × 8 pan-head screws into the inserts; 3. fit the battery tray (its hold-down beams freed: breakaway posts cut): set it 2 mm aft of its place, slide it forward so its three spring fingers ride up their lead-ins onto the board's top face between the rear connectors, screw it down, and check each finger stands lifted: a 0.05 mm feeler does not pass under its tip; if it does, that finger has play (it is off the board): stick 0.1 mm PTFE tape (F03) under its tip as a shim, a layer at a time (about 0.3 mm at most), until the feeler no longer passes; 4. plug the under-carrier cables. Pigtails: dress each one as drawn, with no slack (it rides up with the board when the joint is unplugged): straight up out of the socket, toward the front about 12 mm over the board beside U5A (J9 on the right), out between the P03 and the motor face, and down to the inline joint just ahead of the motor (x 15.2..17.8, |y| 38..60); then trim each wire at its own cavity of the male housing (finished lengths 35.4–60.8 mm for J4 and 31.1–56.5 mm for J5, set by where each wire sits at both ends) and crimp its male pin into the 1×6 housing, red wire = pin 1. Factory cables: measure each one from the encoder cap to the female housing's rear face (the wire entry); readings of 186–200 mm all fit (2–3 turns), and a longer cable up to 220 mm still fits (up to 3.5 turns). Route the fixed path first (about 89 mm outside the coil): a flat row along the motor's inner end face toward the rear, round the motor's rear shoulder and forward over the motor top (never over the pigtail), down the motor's front shoulder under the bumper lead, and from the coil position into the housing; wind the remainder (the measured length less the fixed path: 97–111 mm) into the coil on the base ahead of the motor (2–3.5 turns, about 16 mm across, at x 25, |y| 72) and tie it through its two slots. Then mate each motor's factory female housing onto its pigtail's male housing: the joint is not keyed, so mate the pin-1 stripe to the pin-1 stripe (both halves are marked at the red wire) and check the colours run straight across; stand the joint on the base and tie it down with a cable tie down the motor opening and up through the slot beside it; bumpers J10/J11; front cliffs J8/J9; 5. set and verify the P03 output voltage on the bench, connect it to U5A/U5B (pin 1 is "+" on both terminals, silk "+", the screw nearer the robot centre line: U5A.1 to P03 IN+, U5B.1 to P03 OUT+, red wires on pin 1), then fit it on its foam tape in the front bay with the cable tie through the P_base slots at (28, ±33.3); before the Jetson is connected (W04 unplugged): battery in, F1 fitted, rocker on, and measure against a GND pad: U5A.1 reads positive, about the pack voltage, and U5B.1 positive 5.1 V (0 V or negative: the P03 leads are swapped or loose); then rocker off; 6. stand the two rear 20 mm F-F standoffs on the board and screw each down with an M2.5 × 12 countersunk screw from under P_base through the base, the clamp spacer and the board (they clamp the board); 7. fit the Jetson (four M2.5 top screws), then its six plugs; before the 5 V barrel plug goes in, check the Jetson lead W04 on J3 with its barrel plug free and the rocker on: the plug's centre reads positive 5.1 V against its sleeve (negative: the two Micro-Fit crimps are swapped), then rocker off and plug it in. Service: step 0, every time, before reaching inside: shut the Jetson down, switch the rocker off and unplug the battery (BAT+ is live and unfused at F1's input whenever the battery is plugged in). Everyday rule: the rocker off before plugging or unplugging the battery; shut the Jetson down before switching the rocker off; fit or pull a fuse only with the rocker off (rocker off, fit F2, rocker on). With the lid off, the board's rear band (Pico USB, rear connector row, the Jetson 5 V lead J3, fuses) is reachable; the motor inline joints, the other under-carrier connectors and the P03 (tie, trimpot) need the Jetson off (its six plugs: camera, LiDAR and Pico USB, Wi-Fi dongle, 5 V barrel plug, fan; then its four top screws). To take the board out: Jetson off; the two rear standoffs off (their M2.5 screws from under P_base); the battery out (strap, Tamiya plug); the four tray screws out, the tray slid 2 mm aft and lifted straight out (its springs come off the board edge; its walls are cut clear of the rear cliff sensor boards); the four M3 board screws out; unplug the rear-band plugs, the motor inline joints (loosen each factory-cable coil tie first: the 8 mm each housing slides back comes out of the coil; then cut the joint ties and slide each factory housing off its pigtail; the pigtails stay on J4 / J5 and ride up with the board), the bumper and front cliff leads and the P03 leads; lift the board. Fit new ties when it goes back (retie the coils).

parts.item: M3 × 6 button-head motor-face screws (ISO 7380)
parts.notes: Button heads (1.65 mm) sit in 1 mm counterbores in the motor mount: 1.85 mm to the wheel disc. Nominal engagement 4 mm; motor threaded holes are 6 mm deep. Never use longer screws without checking depth.

parts.item: Bumper guide hardware
parts.notes: Per robot (two 90° arc bumper halves, each floating 5 mm along its own axis 30° inward of rearward): six M3 × 35 countersunk screws (DIN 7991) fixed in the printed rails and arms from below; four 693ZZ ball bearings (3 × 8 × 4 mm) for the rail pins, each between a Ø3.2 × Ø4.5 × 1.5 mm and a Ø3.2 × Ø4.5 × 1 mm stainless spacer (no wider than the inner-ring land) under an M3 thin clamp nut (DIN 439, medium threadlocker); two Ø5 × 6.5 mm sleeves (M3 bore) under a thin clamp nut for pin C; six printed floating riders, each with a brass stop tube (Ø4 × 0.35 wall × 5 mm), a compression spring (music wire, Ø5 OD × 0.5 wire, free length 7.1 mm, about 2.0 N/mm), an Ø7 washer and an M3 nyloc nut: tighten the nyloc until a 0.1 mm feeler just fits between the washer and the stop tube (4.0 N preload per pin, zero vertical play at rest). Eighteen Ø4 mm chrome-steel balls (G10, plus spares): three per half in the rail/arm-top pockets and six per half under the riders. Every ball runs between 0.5 mm hardened spring-steel races (blue-tempered 1095 or AISI 420, ≥ HRC 48, about 0.35 m of 12.7 mm strip, epoxy): eighteen 3.6 × 8 mm strips bonded to P_base (under each down-ball track and on the base top beside each slot) and eighteen 4 × 9 mm strips in the 11.5 mm pocket floors and rider pocket ceilings. Four M2 × 14 screws, washers and nuts for the two switches. Bearing slots in P_base are printed 8.2 mm wide and filed to 8.1–8.2 mm with P_coupon as the gauge (±0.05–0.1 mm side play: the planar-play checks use 0.1). Critical vertical friction ≥ 0.17 over the whole 0–90° arc at 20–98.5 mm, and ≥ 0.08 with bearing and ball friction equal (validation.json bumper_travel.friction_lock, .hertz).

parts.item: Motor pigtails (2): Sullins PPPC061LGBN-RC 1×6 right-angle female socket (board end, wires up) + Pololu 1905 1×6 crimp housing with male pins (joint end) + six 28 AWG silicone wires
parts.source: Sullins PPPC061LGBN-RC via Digi-Key / Mouser; Pololu 1905 housings and male crimp pins (pololu.com); a 6-colour 28 AWG silicone wire set
parts.notes: One per motor (ruling PB25 amended; B9). Board end: Sullins PPPC061LGBN-RC: 1x6 2.54 mm right-angle female socket header, through-hole (2.54 mm insulator lying on the board, 8.51 mm deep, tails 3.15 mm; verify), pushed onto J4 / J5's right-angle pins with its six solder tails pointing upward; each wire is lapped 2 mm on a tail tip and soldered under a Ø1.8 mm heat-shrink sleeve, so the wires leave the board upward (socket 2.54 mm tall on the board, tails and sleeves to 8.19 mm over it, inside the 16.27 mm under-carrier zone; the socket and the wires' exit stay 3.2 mm off the motor face) and turn over at >= 3.1 mm radius for the innermost wire (>= 3 × the 1 mm insulation OD). Joint end: a Pololu 1905 1×6 0.1 in crimp housing with six male crimp pins (or a 1×6 straight male header with the wires soldered on if no DuPont crimper). Wire: six 28 AWG silicone wires (Ø1.0 mm), colour-coded red, black, green, blue, yellow, white = pins 1-6 (pins 1-2, the motor pair: 26 AWG thin-wall PTFE / ETFE, OD <= 1.0 mm, preferred if available), in the factory cable's colour order. Pre-cut length = the drawn route + 8.5 mm of terminations (2 lapped on the tail, 2.5 in the sleeve past the tip, 4 in the crimp housing) + the full 12.7 mm pin spread (the six wires fan out 6.35 mm either side of the drawn Ø3 bundle axis at the socket's sleeves and again at the male housing's cavities), rounded up to the mm: left (J4) 61 mm, right (J5) 57 mm per wire. Built alike: looking into the socket's mating face with its tails up, the red wire is on the left (pin 1 on J4's rear end, J5's front end). Polarity: the inline joint is not keyed, so pin 1 is marked on both halves: a paint-pen stripe on the pigtail's male housing at the red wire and on the factory female housing at its red wire; mate stripe to stripe and check the colours run straight across. Each joint is tied down on P_base and the factory cable's spare length is coiled and tied (C12 ties; assembly step 4). They stay with the board. parts.item: Camera LED inline switch: Microchip TN0702N3-G MOSFET (TO-92), 39 Ω 0.25 W, 100 Ω and 100 kΩ resistors, heat-shrink
parts.notes: Task N (LIO-134). Built inline in the LED lead W21 on the bench, before the bay board goes in; the routed board does not change. Circuit: J15 hole 5 (5 V) → 39 Ω 0.25 W → LED anode; LED cathode → MOSFET drain; MOSFET source → J15 hole 6 (GND); MOSFET gate ← 100 Ω ← J15 hole 3 (GP20 (SPARE3)); 100 kΩ from gate to source keeps the LED off while the Pico boots or resets. Current: (5 − 2.7 V) / 39 Ω = 59 mA, inside the 0.10 A budget of J15 pin 5; 0.16 W in the LED, 0.14 W in the 39 Ω, about 0.30 W in all. The three wires are soldered into J15 (no header: a mated housing would not fit under the Jetson carrier); the switch sits in heat-shrink in the front bay, past the carrier's front edge, each joint in its own sleeve and the bundle in one more. Check the TN0702N3-G pin order (TO-92) against the datasheet before soldering. About USD 3: estimate, verify.
